title: Sunset fine-tune compatibility layer and client adaptation PRD
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: PRD to deprecate the legacy fine-tune compatibility layer (FT-compat) used by older clients and internal runtimes. The FT-compat shim translates historical fine-tune-style requests into the unified inference request shape. We will phase out FT-compat across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while providing client adapters, telemetry gates, and clear rollback criteria.
background: FT-compat was introduced in 2022 to accelerate customer adoption of fine-tune flows. Since the unified inference API launched, FT-compat increases complexity in the runtime, produces subtle behavioral differences (KV handling, prompt trimming), and prevents certain kernel optimizations. Several infra and product teams have requested removal to reduce maintenance cost and unlock batching/quantization regressions.
goals: 1) Remove FT-compat shim without impacting critical customers. 2) Provide clear client migration helpers and an SDK adapter that preserves common patterns. 3) Ensure parity of outputs for top 95% of customer prompt shapes. 4) Reduce FT-compat code surface by 100% in hosted runtime by the target release.
out_of_scope: Full migration of custom user training pipelines and archival legacy on-prem deploys that require contract extension. Migration of third-party vendor tooling that wraps FT-compat (customers must update their tooling).
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK adapters released (JS/Python/Go) with automated conversion tests and example patterns documented. 2) Canary traffic shows <=1% error spike and output drift within defined thresholds for 95% of test prompts. 3) >=75% of active customers who used FT-compat have integrated the adapter or validated equivalence in shadow mode. 4) Host runtime no longer executes FT-compat code paths for non-shadow requests in runtime-2.4 GA. 5) Rollback playbook and emergency toggle exist and tested in staging.
rollout_timeline: Phase 0 (Announcement): 2026-03-22 - public blog, customer emails, deprecation FAQ. Phase 1 (Adapter SDKs & Docs): 2026-04-05 - publish JS/Python/Go adapters and migration guide. Phase 2 (Shadow Mode & Telemetry): 2026-04-19 - enable shadow translation by default for hosted accounts; gather drift metrics. Phase 3 (Canary): 2026-05-03 - route 1% traffic through new path with graceback to compatibility when gates fail. Phase 4 (Gradual Cutover): 2026-05-17 - expand to 25%/50%/100% based on telemetry gates. Phase 5 (Sunset): 2026-06-01 - disable FT-compat in hosted; customers on Dedicated/Private have a 90-day custom window starting this date.
migration_strategy: Provide lightweight SDK adapters and a CLI validation tool that runs customers' canonical prompts against both FT-compat and unified API, emitting a drift report. Offer an opt-in compatibility gateway for Dedicated/Private customers during the 90-day extension. Coordinate with Account Success for top-50 customers to provide migration engineering time.
tasks: Draft customer-facing deprecation announcement and FAQ
Build JS/Python/Go adapter packages and publish to NPM/PyPI
Create CLI 'compat-validate' tool and migration report schema
Add shadow translation hook and drift telemetry in hosted runtime
Define output-drift metric and alert thresholds with Research/QA
Implement runtime gate toggles and canary routing configuration
Prepare rollback runbooks and simulate rollback in staging
Coordinate Dedicated/Private deployment playbooks with Solutions Eng
Instrument SDK usage telemetry to track adoption
Run cross-team tabletop with Legal, Security, and Support
risks_mitigations: Risk: Output drift causes customer-visible regressions -> Mitigation: shadow mode, drift thresholds, gated canary and targeted rollbacks
Risk: Large on-prem customers cannot upgrade quickly -> Mitigation: offer 90-day Dedicated/Private extension and engineering assistance
Risk: SDK adapter misses edge-case encodings -> Mitigation: comprehensive test suite, fuzzing harness, and community preview program
Risk: Missing telemetry prevents safe cutover -> Mitigation: block cutover until coverage gates met and alerting is verified
decisions: 1) Remove FT-compat code paths from hosted runtime first (fastest ROI), 2) Provide opt-in extension for Dedicated/Private customers, 3) Require SDK adapters to be published for GA cutover, 4) Use shadow mode + drift gating as primary safety mechanism.
monitoring_and_gates: Define 'drift_ratio' = percentage of outputs that exceed Research-defined token-level divergence per prompt family. Cutover gates: drift_ratio < 5% and error_rate_change < 1% over 48h for canary. Telemetry dashboards: per-route drift, per-customer adoption, SDK install counts.
notes_and_comments: 2026-02-25: Initial scoping call with runtime, SDK, and Solutions Eng. 2026-03-01: Research defined drift thresholds for prompt families 'short-completions' and 'structured-insert'. 2026-03-12: Legal reviewed deprecation notice language and requested explicit SLA notes for Dedicated customers.
customer_communication_plan: 1) Email wave 1 to customers with FT-compat usage metrics and migration kit (2026-03-22). 2) Host migration office hours weekly (Apr-May). 3) Account Success outreach for top-50 customers with migration offers. 4) Final sunset reminder 30/14/7 days before hosted sunset.
rollback_criteria: If canary shows drift_ratio >= 10% or spike in user errors > 3x baseline for 1 hour, immediately pause and rollback to FT-compat. Documented runbook exists and was run in staging.
open_questions: 1) What is the commercial credit policy for customers who must extend Dedicated compatibility windows? 2) Should adapter packages include automatic telemetry opt-in by default? 3) How do we version the migration report schema to support iterative improvements?
